summary: This diff (PR #562, all three rounds) adds a 4-layer defense-in-depth prompt-security module and, in its round-2 fix, correctly closes the two real enforcement gaps a prior audit found: Layer 3's Llama Guard input/output calls now fail CLOSED (block, with an explicit console.error) on a network/API error instead of silently defaulting to a permissive 'safe' verdict, and a genuine Layer 4 leaked-system-instruction detection now actually blocks the reply (blocked: true, content: '') instead of being computed and discarded. Verified directly against the committed HEAD (058a2619) source rather than the self-report: defense-in-depth.ts's block paths, the route.ts wiring (usage! is safe since it's only read after the blocked branch already returned), pii-redaction.ts's new shared findPii()/redactPii() core, and layer4's SSN/US-phone additions all read correctly and the type imports (LLMUsage/CallLLMOptions/LLMFallback) resolve against llm-client.ts's real exports. Two real but non-blocking issues remain (see issues list): a duplicated 'scope_note' YAML key introduced in ai-os/boss/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml in three unrelated, pre-existing entries (SUPERBOSS_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v2, PROJEXA veri-chat, drizzle renumbering) that has nothing to do with this task's scope, and Layer 1's 'suspicious' verdict tier being a documented no-op (defense-in-depth.ts only special-cases 'malicious', so 'suspicious' currently behaves identically to 'benign' with no real downstream scrutiny). Diff does not touch .github/workflows/**. Recommend a human merge given tier2 (path contains 'prompt-security'/'security').
issues: ai-os/boss/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml: this diff adds a duplicate `scope_note:` mapping key (at a shallower 4-space indent, immediately followed by unchanged pre-existing content with the same key at 6-space indent and near-identical text) in three separate, unrelated `recently_completed` entries -- SUPERBOSS_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-07-19_v2 (~line 5682), the PROJEXA veri-chat entry (~line 5792), and the drizzle-migration-renumbering entry (~line 5831). None of these three entries are related to phase4-defense-in-depth-prompt-security. Duplicate keys in the same YAML mapping are undefined/parser-dependent behavior and risk breaking any strict YAML consumer of this coordination file (e.g. sync-controller-back.py). Should be de-duplicated in a follow-up commit before/after merge.

Layer 1's 3-way verdict (benign/suspicious/malicious) is only actually enforced as a 2-way gate in practice: runDefenseInDepth() only blocks on verdict === 'malicious'; a 'suspicious' verdict (e.g. from Prompt Guard 2 flagging MALICIOUS while the deterministic check found nothing) proceeds through the pipeline identically to 'benign', with no extra scrutiny actually implemented anywhere downstream despite the type comment's claim that 'suspicious' is 'flagged for downstream scrutiny'. Not a regression from this round's changes, but worth a follow-up if the second-opinion classifier is meant to carry real weight.

Pre-existing local workspace note (not part of the pushed PR -- verified the remote branch HEAD matches this session's local HEAD exactly, commit 058a2619): this task workspace's git index currently has large staged-but-uncommitted changes reverting defense-in-depth.ts's fail-closed/leak-blocking logic and touching many unrelated files. This does not affect the real PR #562 diff under review, but whoever next uses this on-disk workspace should not blindly `git commit`/`git push` from it without first inspecting `git diff --cached`.
